AUTHOR: Zhang, D; Kopanas, G; Desai, C; Chai, S; Piacentino, M
TITLE: Unsupervised Underwater Fish Detection Fusing Flow and Objectiveness
VENUE: 2016 IEEE WINTER APPLICATIONS OF COMPUTER VISION WORKSHOPS (WACVW)
V_EV: Sec 4.1: 'We have used optical flow to detect fish in the hazy underwater environment in which objects about 10 meters away are obscured.'
D2: train: samples from first 20 min of one sequence; test: video from a different camera
D_EV: Sec 5: '100,000 samples were generated from the first 20 minutes of video. Fish detection was tested from a different camera monitoring the same area.'
R_EV: Sec 5: 'Fish detection was tested from a different camera monitoring the same area.' (same area/campaign; not a different camera system per P2)
C_EV: Sec 5: 'Detection scores are displayed in 7(d). A simple threshold removes negative scores.'
E_EV: Sec 5: only AP reported, 'AP of the Selective Search only = 56%, and AP of the fused proposal (green curve) = 66%.'
ARCH: CaffeNet (AlexNet) R-CNN-style classifier on Selective Search + optical-flow proposals, modified NMS
NOTE: Platform/location of NOAA videos not stated. 'Different camera monitoring the same area' treated as same campaign (R1=N); could be argued as camera domain shift. Threshold implied at 0 (negative scores removed) -> C1=Y, default. Visibility statement (~10 m) is descriptive, not measured; coded qualitative. Modified NMS addresses duplicate boxes per frame, not duplicate counts -> C5 none.
